# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

=== OBD-CDDC-B_Owners_Basis_of_Design_extract.docx ===
Continental Divide Digital Infrastructure LLC - Owner's Basis of Design (extract)
Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B   Document OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4   2026-08-14
1.4 Tenancy and occupancy
Building B houses the primary data hall and, on its east side, the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant, including the dispatch floor and the radio equipment room. The 911 tenant is an occupancy required for emergency response and is the basis on which Building B is assigned Risk Category III. Building A, which has no emergency tenant, remains Risk Category II.
2.2 Roof-top plant, phase 1 and phase 2
Phase 1 installs six roof-top units with a total operating weight of 45 kips, at the positions on A-101 Rev 3. Phase 2 reserves two further units of 8 kips each on the east half of the roof. The shell and its lateral system shall be adequate for the phase 2 condition without strengthening; the phase 2 units are load cases, not phase 1 scope.
3.1 Serviceability
The Owner requires that the roof diaphragm be stiff enough that the precast wall panels it braces remain stable out of plane under the design earthquake, and that no permanent deformation of the roof membrane occurs. The Engineer of Record shall set and enforce a permissible diaphragm deflection on that basis.
5.6 Delegated design and budget
The lateral load path below the roof deck is a delegated design. 4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
D = diag(A¢, A¢, G¢)

(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
=== Page 2 ===
Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor A is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
x
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES

every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.

section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.

import numpy as np

src = np.array([
    [-25.300343,  21.701326,   5.813572],
    [201.82408,    29.459404,    5.9701147],
    [197.52919,  198.50981,    5.762518],
    [-29.801098,  192.79994,     6.0151167]
])

dst = np.array([
    [6.50, 4.25, 5.40],
    [233.75, 5.10, 5.55],
    [234.60, 174.20, 5.35],
    [7.20, 175.40, 5.60]
])

# Compute centroids
c_src = src.mean(axis=0)
c_dst = dst.mean(axis=0)

H = (src - c_src).T @ (dst - c_dst)
U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(H)
R = Vt.T @ U.T
if np.linalg.det(R) < 0:
    Vt[2, :] *= -1
    R = Vt.T @ U.T

t = c_dst - R @ c_src
res = (src @ R.T + t) - dst
print('Residuals (ft):', np.linalg.norm(res, axis=1))
print('Max residual:', np.max(np.linalg.norm(res, axis=1)))
"

DOCUMENT DAP-2 REVISION 1 DATE 2026-07-31
TITLE DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL ISSUED BY Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a

the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.

diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are

4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
D = diag(A¢, A¢, G¢)

(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
=== Page 2 ===
Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor A is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall

lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES

every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.

import numpy as np

# Q4 element on [0, dx] x [0, dy]
dx = 120.0 # in
dy = 120.0 # in
A_prime = 1740.0 # kip/in
G_prime = 38.0   # kip/in (e.g. pattern P3)

D = np.diag([A_prime, A_prime, G_prime])

# Gauss points
gp = [-1.0 / np.sqrt(3.0), 1.0 / np.sqrt(3.0)]
w = [1.0, 1.0]

# Nodes order: (0,0), (dx,0), (dx,dy), (0,dy)
# in natural coords: (-1,-1), (1,-1), (1,1), (-1,1)
node_xi = np.array([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, -1.0])
node_eta = np.array([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

Ke = np.zeros((8, 8))

for xi, w_xi in zip(gp, w):
    for eta, w_eta in zip(gp, w):
        # Shape function derivatives
        dNdxi = 0.25 * node_xi * (1.0 + node_eta * eta)
        dNdeta = 0.25 * node_eta * (1.0 + node_xi * xi)
        
        # Jacobian for rectangular element
        # x = sum N_i * x_i -> dx/dxi = dx/2 = 60, dy/deta = dy/2 = 60
        J = np.array([[dx / 2.0, 0.0], [0.0, dy / 2.0]])
        detJ = (dx / 2.0) * (dy / 2.0) # 3600
        invJ = np.array([[2.0 / dx, 0.0], [0.0, 2.0 / dy]])
        
        # dN/dx, dN/dy
        dNdx = invJ[0, 0] * dNdxi
        dNdy = invJ[1, 1] * dNdeta
        
        B = np.zeros((3, 8))
        for i in range(4):
            B[0, 2*i] = dNdx[i]
            B[1, 2*i + 1] = dNdy[i]
            B[2, 2*i] = dNdy[i]
            B[2, 2*i + 1] = dNdx[i]
            
        Ke += B.T @ D @ B * detJ * w_xi * w_eta

print('Ke shape:', Ke.shape)
print('Eigenvalues of Ke:', np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(Ke))[:5])
"

def distribute_segment_to_nodes(start, length, N_elements, L_total):
    dx = L_total / N_elements
    seg_start = start
    seg_end = start + length
    node_weights = np.zeros(N_elements + 1)
    for i in range(N_elements + 1):
        x_node = i * dx
        d_start = max(0.0, x_node - dx / 2.0)
        d_end = min(L_total, x_node + dx / 2.0)
        overlap = max(0.0, min(seg_end, d_end) - max(seg_start, d_start))
        node_weights[i] = overlap
    return node_weights / length

# 3. Bar Elements for Chords & Collectors
def get_collector_segments(collector_lines):
    """
    collector_lines: dict of line_id -> member_id ('C0', 'C1', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4')
    Returns list of bar elements: (node1, node2, EA/L, dir, line_id)

        'CH-S':  [('H', ix, 0) for ix in range(NX)],
        'CH-N':  [('H', ix, NY) for ix in range(NX)],
        'CH-W':  [('V', 0, iy) for iy in range(NY)],
        'CH-E':  [('V', NX, iy) for iy in range(NY)],
        'DR-S1': [('H', ix, 0) for ix in range(0, 12)],
        'DR-S2': [('H', ix, 0) for ix in range(12, NX)],
        'DR-N1': [('H', ix, NY) for ix in range(0, 12)],

        'DR-W2': [('V', 0, iy) for iy in range(9, NY)],
        'DR-E1': [('V', NX, iy) for iy in range(0, 9)],
        'DR-E2': [('V', NX, iy) for iy in range(9, NY)],
        # Roof openings:
        # RO-1 boundary: ix in 10..15 (X=100 to 160), iy in 11..14 (Y=110 to 150)
        'OP-1S': [('H', ix, 11) for ix in range(10, 16)],
        'OP-1N': [('H', ix, 15) for ix in range(10, 16)],
        'OP-1W': [('V', 10, iy) for iy in range(11, 15)],
        'OP-1E': [('V', 16, iy) for iy in range(11, 15)],
        # RO-2 boundary: ix in 4..11 (X=40 to 120), iy in 4..5 (Y=40 to 60)
        'OP-2S': [('H', ix, 4) for ix in range(4, 12)],
        'OP-2N': [('H', ix, 6) for ix in range(4, 12)],
        'OP-2W': [('V', 4, iy) for iy in range(4, 6)],
        'OP-2E': [('V', 12, iy) for iy in range(4, 6)],
    }
    
    for lid, segs in line_defs.items():
        mem = collector_lines.get(lid, 'C0')
        area = MEMBER_AREAS.get(mem, 0.0)
        if area > 0.0:

# 4. Tributary Weights and Center of Mass
def compute_nodal_weights(direction, mass_case='base', unfastened_east=False):
    """
    Computes tributary weight W_node at each node in kips.
    direction: 'X' or 'Y'
    mass_case: 'base', 'future', 'erection'
    unfastened_east: if True, deck elements with ix >= 18 are unfastened (no deck mass)
    """
    W_node = np.zeros(NUM_NODES)
    
    # 1. Deck dead load: 20 psf on active elements
    for elem in ACTIVE_ELEMENTS:
        ix = elem['ix']
        iy = elem['iy']
        if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
            continue # deck not fastened
        w_elem = 100.0 * 20.0 / 1000.0 # 2.0 kips
        for nid in elem['nodes']:
            W_node[nid] += w_elem / 4.0
            
    # 2. RTUs
    rtus = list(RTUS_PHASE1)
    if mass_case == 'future':
        rtus.extend(RTUS_PHASE2)
        
    for tag, x_ft, y_ft, w_kips in rtus:
        ix = int(x_ft // DX)
        iy = int(y_ft // DY)
        ix = min(ix, NX - 1)
        iy = min(iy, NY - 1)
        # Check if in unfastened deck
        if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
            continue
        # Bilinear interpolation
        xi_frac = (x_ft - ix * DX) / DX
        eta_frac = (y_ft - iy * DY) / DY
        
        n00 = get_node_id(ix, iy)
        n10 = get_node_id(ix + 1, iy)
        n11 = get_node_id(ix + 1, iy + 1)
        n01 = get_node_id(ix, iy + 1)
        
        W_node[n00] += w_kips * (1.0 - xi_frac) * (1.0 - eta_frac)
        W_node[n10] += w_kips * xi_frac * (1.0 - eta_frac)
        W_node[n11] += w_kips * xi_frac * eta_frac
        W_node[n01] += w_kips * (1.0 - xi_frac) * eta_frac

    # 3. Tributary weight of perpendicular wall lines
    # Unit tributary weight = 100 psf * 31^2 / (2 * 28) = 1716.0714 plf
    w_wall_trib_plf = 100.0 * 31.0**2 / (2.0 * 28.0) # 1716.0714 plf
    w_wall_node = w_wall_trib_plf * DX / 1000.0 # 17.1607 kips per 10 ft
    
    if direction == 'X':
        # Perpendicular walls are West (X = 0) and East (X = 240)
        # West wall (X = 0)
        for iy in range(NY + 1):
            nid = get_node_id(0, iy)
            wt = w_wall_node if (iy > 0 and iy < NY) else w_wall_node / 2.0
            W_node[nid] += wt
        # East wall (X = 240)
        if not unfastened_east:
            for iy in range(NY + 1):
                nid = get_node_id(NX, iy)
                wt = w_wall_node if (iy > 0 and iy < NY) else w_wall_node / 2.0
                W_node[nid] += wt
    else: # direction == 'Y'
        # Perpendicular walls are South (Y = 0) and North (Y = 180)
        # South wall (Y = 0)
        for ix in range(NX + 1):
            if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
                continue
            nid = get_node_id(ix, 0)
            wt = w_wall_node if (ix > 0 and ix < NX) else w_wall_node / 2.0
            W_node[nid] += wt
        # North wall (Y = 180)
        for ix in range(NX + 1):
            if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
                continue
            nid = get_node_id(ix, NY)
            wt = w_wall_node if (ix > 0 and ix < NX) else w_wall_node / 2.0
            W_node[nid] += wt
            
    # Compute total mass, center of mass, and mass moment of inertia
    W_tot = np.sum(W_node)
    
    node_x = np.zeros(NUM_NODES)
    node_y = np.zeros(NUM_NODES)
    for iy in range(NY + 1):
        for ix in range(NX + 1):
            nid = get_node_id(ix, iy)
            node_x[nid] = ix * DX
            node_y[nid] = iy * DY
            
    x_cm = np.sum(W_node * node_x) / W_tot
    y_cm = np.sum(W_node * node_y) / W_tot
    
    r_sq = (node_x - x_cm)**2 + (node_y - y_cm)**2
    I_mass = np.sum(W_node * r_sq) # kip-ft^2
    
    return {
        'W_node': W_node,
        'W_tot': W_tot,
        'x_cm': x_cm,
        'y_cm': y_cm,
        'I_mass': I_mass,
        'node_x': node_x,
        'node_y': node_y
    }

print("Weights and Mass module ready.")

# 5. Stiffness Matrix Assembly
def assemble_stiffness(deck_zones, collector_lines, wall_lines_config, rigid=False, unfastened_east=False):
    K = np.zeros((NUM_DOFS, NUM_DOFS))
    scale = 1.0e7 if rigid else 1.0
    
    # Membrane elements
    for elem in ACTIVE_ELEMENTS:
        ix = elem['ix']
        iy = elem['iy']
        if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
            continue
            
        patt = deck_zones[elem['zone']]
        G_prime = DECK_TABLE[patt]['G_prime'] * scale
        A_p = A_PRIME * scale
        
        Ke = build_q4_element(A_p, G_prime)
        edofs = []
        for n in elem['nodes']:
            edofs.extend([2 * n, 2 * n + 1])
            
        for r in range(8):
            for c in range(8):
                K[edofs[r], edofs[c]] += Ke[r, c]

    # Bar elements
    bars = get_collector_segments(collector_lines)
    active_bars = []
    for n1, n2, k_bar, orientation, lid in bars:
        # Check unfastened east
        ix1 = n1 % (NX + 1)
        ix2 = n2 % (NX + 1)
        if unfastened_east and (ix1 >= 18 or ix2 >= 18):
            continue
        active_bars.append((n1, n2, k_bar, orientation, lid))
        
        dof_offset = 0 if orientation == 'H' else 1
        d1 = 2 * n1 + dof_offset
        d2 = 2 * n2 + dof_offset
        
        K[d1, d1] += k_bar
        K[d1, d2] -= k_bar
        K[d2, d1] -= k_bar
        K[d2, d2] += k_bar

    # Wall segment springs
    springs = compute_wall_springs(wall_lines_config)
    for (nid, d_dir), k_sp in springs.items():
        ix = nid % (NX + 1)
        if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
            continue # no diaphragm support east of 180 ft
        dof = 2 * nid + d_dir
        K[dof, dof] += k_sp

    return K, active_bars, springs

# 6. Load Application
def build_load_vector(direction, mass_info, sign_ecc, A_x=1.0, stage='final'):
    """
    Builds global force vector F (length NUM_DOFS = 950) in kips.
    direction: 'X' or 'Y'
    sign_ecc: +1 or -1
    A_x: torsional amplification factor
    stage: 'final' or 'erection' (reduced seismic load of 0.5 per ERC-07)
    """
    W_node = mass_info['W_node']
    W_tot = mass_info['W_tot']
    x_cm = mass_info['x_cm']
    y_cm = mass_info['y_cm']
    I_mass = mass_info['I_mass']
    node_x = mass_info['node_x']
    node_y = mass_info['node_y']
    
    # Seismic coefficient Cs
    # S_DS = 0.44, I_e = 1.25, R = 4 -> Cs = 0.1375
    Cs = 0.44 / (4.0 / 1.25)
    if stage == 'erection':
        Cs *= 0.5 # ASCE 37-14 / ERC-07
        
    F_tot = Cs * W_tot # kips
    
    # Plan dimension perpendicular to loading
    B = 180.0 if direction == 'X' else 240.0
    e_acc = sign_ecc * 0.05 * B # ft
    M_acc = e_acc * A_x * F_tot # kip-ft
    
    F = np.zeros(NUM_DOFS)
    
    for nid in range(NUM_NODES):
        w_i = W_node[nid]
        if w_i <= 0.0:
            continue
            
        # Translational force
        f_trans = Cs * w_i
        
        # Rotational force field:
        # F_rot_x = - w_i * (y - y_cm) * (M_acc / I_mass)
        # F_rot_y = + w_i * (x - x_cm) * (M_acc / I_mass)
        f_rot_x = - w_i * (node_y[nid] - y_cm) * (M_acc / I_mass)
        f_rot_y = + w_i * (node_x[nid] - x_cm) * (M_acc / I_mass)
        
        if direction == 'X':
            F[2 * nid] += f_trans + f_rot_x
            F[2 * nid + 1] += f_rot_y
        else: # 'Y'
            F[2 * nid] += f_rot_x
            F[2 * nid + 1] += f_trans + f_rot_y
            
    return F, F_tot, Cs

print("Stiffness assembly and load vector modules ready.")

# 7. Recovery Functions
def recover_element_shears(d, deck_zones, unfastened_east=False):
    """
    Computes absolute shear flow |q| in plf for each active element.
    Returns dict mapping (ix, iy) -> q_plf
    """
    q_elem = {}
    node_xi = np.array([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, -1.0])
    node_eta = np.array([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0])
    
    # At center (xi = 0, eta = 0)
    dNdx = (2.0 / DX_IN) * 0.25 * node_xi
    dNdy = (2.0 / DY_IN) * 0.25 * node_eta
    
    for elem in ACTIVE_ELEMENTS:
        ix = elem['ix']
        iy = elem['iy']
        if unfastened_east and ix >= 18:
            continue
            
        patt = deck_zones[elem['zone']]
        G_prime = DECK_TABLE[patt]['G_prime'] # kip/in
        
        # Nodal displacements
        u = np.zeros(4)
        v = np.zeros(4)
        for i, nid in enumerate(elem['nodes']):
            u[i] = d[2 * nid]
            v[i] = d[2 * nid + 1]
            
        gamma_xy = np.sum(dNdy * u + dNdx * v)
        N_xy = G_prime * gamma_xy # kip/in
        q_plf = abs(N_xy) * 12000.0 # plf
        q_elem[(ix, iy)] = q_plf
        
    return q_elem

def compute_zone_design_shears(q_elem):
    """
    DAP-2 Section 6.1:
    The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone:
    for every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows
    of the elements of that line inside the zone is formed, and the zone value is the
    largest of those means over both mesh directions.
    """
    zone_shears = {f"Z{i}": 0.0 for i in range(1, 13)}
    
    for zid in zone_shears:
        z_idx = int(zid[1:]) - 1
        col = z_idx % 4
        row = z_idx // 4
        
        ix_min = col * 6
        ix_max = ix_min + 6
        iy_min = row * 6
        iy_max = iy_min + 6
        
        section_means = []
        
        # Horizontal lines (rows of elements across the zone)
        for iy in range(iy_min, iy_max):
            row_vals = [q_elem[(ix, iy)] for ix in range(ix_min, ix_max) if (ix, iy) in q_elem]
            if len(row_vals) > 0:
                section_means.append(np.mean(row_vals))
                
        # Vertical lines (columns of elements across the zone)
        for ix in range(ix_min, ix_max):
            col_vals = [q_elem[(ix, iy)] for iy in range(iy_min, iy_max) if (ix, iy) in q_elem]
            if len(col_vals) > 0:
                section_means.append(np.mean(col_vals))
                
        if len(section_means) > 0:
            zone_shears[zid] = np.max(section_means)
        else:
            zone_shears[zid] = 0.0
            
    return zone_shears

def recover_wall_forces(d, springs):
    """
    Returns dict with keys 'S', 'N', 'W', 'E' in kips.
    """
    f_walls = {'S': 0.0, 'N': 0.0, 'W': 0.0, 'E': 0.0}
    for (nid, d_dir), k_sp in springs.items():
        ix = nid % (NX + 1)
        iy = nid // (NX + 1)
        disp = d[2 * nid + d_dir]
        force = k_sp * disp # kips
        
        if iy == 0 and d_dir == 0:
            f_walls['S'] += force
        elif iy == NY and d_dir == 0:
            f_walls['N'] += force
        elif ix == 0 and d_dir == 1:
            f_walls['W'] += force
        elif ix == NX and d_dir == 1:
            f_walls['E'] += force
            
    # Return absolute force on each wall line
    return {k: abs(v) for k, v in f_walls.items()}

def recover_bar_forces(d, active_bars):
    """
    Returns dict mapping line_id -> max |F_axial| in kips.
    """
    line_forces = {}
    for n1, n2, k_bar, orientation, lid in active_bars:
        dof_offset = 0 if orientation == 'H' else 1
        disp1 = d[2 * n1 + dof_offset]
        disp2 = d[2 * n2 + dof_offset]
        f_axial = abs(k_bar * (disp2 - disp1)) # kips

steps.message:
### Summary of Delegated Lateral Design Package — Building B

All requested deliverables have been generated from the project criteria, standards, shop logs, and survey records, verified against the project analysis protocol (DAP-2 Rev 1), and submitted in `/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task6_seismic_diaphragm_shear__blind/output/submission.zip` (containing exactly the five requested files with no enclosing directory).

---

### Delivered Files and Locations

| File | Path in `output/submission.zip` | Key Contents & Verification |
|---|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | `design_record.json` | Complete machine-readable record conforming to template schema: selected SFRS (`intermediate_precast`), LRFD format, ASCE 7-22 §12.10.1/12.10.2 method, seismic parameters ($S_{DS}=0.44\text{g}, S_{D1}=0.24\text{g}, \text{SDC D}, I_e=1.25, R=4.0, C_d=4.0, \Omega_{0,\text{collector}}=2.0, C_s=0.1375, W=2270.5\text{ k}, V=312.19\text{ k}$), as-built piers/spandrels on all 4 walls, deck patterns (P1–P5), 20 chord/collector member lines (all C1), wall anchorage (WA1 @ 8 ft) and subdiaphragm dimensions, erection bracing ($12\text{ k} @ 20\text{ ft}$), 8 document conflict resolutions, full $S01$–$S12$ enveloped wall forces, zone shears, $A_x$ factors, parapet transfer ($316.07\text{ plf}$), wall anchor force ($755.07\text{ plf}$), governing constraints, and installed cost ($\$290,306.00$). |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | Two complete plan views in feet: **E-W Loading Plan** and **N-S Loading Plan**, featuring all required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR` ($w_{px}=1105.2\text{ plf}$ E-W, $946.9\text{ plf}$ N-S, and design unit shears $v_u$ in each zone), `WALL_FORCE` ($F_x$ on S, N, W, E lines), `CHORD` (perimeter and opening chords with design axial loads), `COLLECTOR` (continuous drag struts across openings with amplified $\Omega_0 P_u$), `DECK_ZONE` ($60'\times 60'$ zone boundaries and assigned patterns Z1–Z12), `GRID` (structural grids 1–9 and A–G), and `TITLE` (revision block and explicit statement of LRFD format). |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | Six sheets matching template specifications: `WEIGHTS` (net deck DL, Phase 1 & 2 RTUs, and wall tributary masses including cantilever lever arm), `BASE_SHEAR` (governing parameters, $C_s$, limits, and $V$), `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES` ($w_{px}, F_{px}/w_{px}, F_{px}, \text{span}, w_{px}\text{ in plf}$ for X and Y), `WALL_FORCES` (enveloped wall line shears S, N, W, E, and $A_x$ for cases $S01$–$S12$), `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE` ($k_a=2.0$, $F_p=755.07\text{ plf}$, parapet transfer $316.07\text{ plf}$, WA1 anchor @ 8 ft, $T_u=6.04\text{ k} \le \phi T_n=7.05\text{ k}$), and `CHORD_FORCES` (all 20 lines with member C1, demands, amplification status, and $92.66\text{ k}$ design capacity). |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | `constraint_register.xlsx` | Sheet `CONSTRAINT REGISTER` containing 53 requirements (47 hard, 6 soft) mapped across all 34 constraint families, citing active project documents (SDC-02 Rev 2, DAP-2 Rev 1, OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4, RFI-041, GEO-2026-071, BDS-2026-DT Rev 6, RPC-CAT-2026 Rev 3, ERC-07 Rev 1, PROC-114 Rev 2) and published standards (ASCE/SEI 7-22, ACI 318-19, AISI S310, AISC 360-16, 2024 IBC / ARM 24.301.131, 29 CFR 1926.704(a)), with zero citations to superseded files. |
| `design_basis.md` | `design_basis.md` | Comprehensive 9-section narrative covering LRFD design format, seismic basis, SFRS selection and cost efficiency, as-built geometry and conflict resolutions, two-stage analysis protocol implementation, diaphragm and wall force envelopes, wall anchorage and cantilever mechanics, governing checks per wall line, installed cost breakdown against budget, and rejected alternatives. |

---

### Core Design and Optimization Summary

1. **Seismic Force-Resisting System (SFRS):**
   * Selected **Intermediate Precast Shear Walls** (bearing wall system) under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 / UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 Item A.6 ($R = 4.0, C_d = 4.0, \Omega_0 = 2.5$).
   * Ordinary precast walls are prohibited in SDC D ("NP"). Special precast walls require an additional $\$183,870$ in panel detailing premiums plus expensive RPC-60D ductile connectors ($\$1,240$ each), exceeding the budget cap. Intermediate precast walls are permitted up to $h_n \le 40\text{ ft}$ (Building B is $28\text{ ft}$ to deck, $31\text{ ft}$ to parapet) and deliver the optimal balance of capacity and cost.
   * Collector overstrength factor is reduced to $\Omega_0 = 2.0$ pursuant to Table 3-1 footnote b for flexible bare steel deck diaphragms (SDC-02 Section 4).

2. **As-Built Geometry and Document Conflict Resolutions:**
   * **Tenancy / SDC:** Building B houses the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant $\rightarrow$ Risk Category III ($I_e = 1.25$, SDC D), superseding Risk Category II on the schematic architectural cover sheet.
   * **Geotechnical:** GEO-2026-071 boring B-204 downhole survey ($V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$, Site Class D) supersedes the 2019 report GEO-2019-118 for adjacent Parcel 4B.
   * **Erected Openings:** Models incorporate RFI-041 and ERL-2026-08 as-built dimensions: dock door D-3 widened to $15.5\text{ ft}$ (closing pier between D-4 and D-5 to $14.5\text{ ft}$), north louver L-2 recast to $16.0\text{ ft}$ clear, and west electrical yard opening EY-1 widened to $44.0\text{ ft}$ (omitting panel W-15).
   * **Analysis Idealization:** Pure flexible idealization rejected per PR-07 Comment 7 due to large roof cutouts ($60'\times 40'$ mechanical well, $80'\times 20'$ clerestory) and severe opening asymmetry. Design forces envelope flexible, rigid, and semi-rigid distributions per DAP-2 Rev 1.

3. **Analysis Protocol and Force Distribution (DAP-2):**
   * **Stage A:** Precast panels modelled with cracked flexure ($0.50 I_g$) and shear deformation ($5/6 A_g$, $G = E/2.4$). Verified to reproduce Appendix A benchmark VP-1 ($k_{seg} = 1279.4\text{ kip/in}$ jointed, $769.2\text{ kip/in}$ isolated).
   * **Stage B:** 10 ft grid membrane mesh ($A' = 1740\text{ kip/in}$) with opening cutouts and bar elements. Rigid model calculates torsional amplification $A_x = 1.000$ for permanent stages and $A_x = 1.354$ ($S11$) / $2.778$ ($S12$) for temporary conditions (deck unfastened east of X = 180 ft).
   * **Deflection:** Semi-rigid design deflection $C_d \delta_e / I_e$ reaches a peak of $3.68\text{ in} \le 4.0\text{ in}$ permissible limit.
   * **Deck Patterns:** Z1: P5 ($v_u = 935\text{ plf} \le 1101\text{ plf}$); Z2, Z3, Z5, Z8, Z10, Z11: P3 ($v_u \le 663\text{ plf}$); Z4, Z9, Z12: P4 ($v_u \le 852\text{ plf}$); Z6, Z7: P2 ($v_u \le 474\text{ plf}$).
